Requirements for Completed Application.- Letter of application- CV- Unofficial copy of transcripts (The selected candidate will be required to submit official copies of transcripts before time of appointment- Three references and their contact information (including a current address, phone number and e-mail address) Posting Details Position Information Job Category Hourly/Adjunct Position Title Adjunct Instructor of Mathematics Working Title Adjunct Instructor of Mathematics Scheduled Hours Per Week FLSA Status Exempt Job Summary Job Summary Concord University’s Department of Mathematics and Computer Science invites applications for adjunct faculty positions in Mathematics.Adjunct instructors will teach introductory mathematics courses—including Quantitative Reasoning, College Algebra, and Elementary Statistics, as well as associated corequisite support sections. Courses may be offered in person on Concord University’s main campus in Athens, WV, and/or online, depending on departmental needs.. Successful candidates will demonstrate a commitment to high‑quality undergraduate instruction, support for student success in foundational mathematics, and alignment with Concord University’s mission of fostering academic excellence and a supportive learning environment. Applicants must hold a master’s degree in Mathematics, Statistics, or a closely related field. Duties and Responsibilities Duty/Responsibility To perform this role successfully, an individual should be able to: Prepare and deliver instruction in introductory mathematics courses in alignment with the established course map, in both in‑person and online formats. Develop and maintain course materials, including syllabi, assignments, and supplemental instructional resources. Assess student learning through assignments, tests, and other evaluations, grading fairly and consistently, and providing timely feedback to support student progress. Contribute to General Education Assessment by collecting, documenting, and reporting required course data. Maintain regular office hours to provide academic support, assist with course‑related questions, and contribute to student recruitment and retention efforts. Keep accurate records of attendance, grades, and other required documentation in compliance with federal FERPA regulations. Perform additional duties as assigned by the Department Chair or Dean. % of Time 100 Education/Knowledge Minimum Education Master's Required Licenses/Certification Master’s degree in Mathematics, Statistics, or a closely related field. Required Skills Solid understanding of introductory mathematics, including quantitative reasoning, algebra, and statistics Strong teaching and communication skills, with the ability to explain concepts clearly to a wide range of learners Ability to create a supportive and engaging learning environment Skill in developing instructional materials and using effective teaching strategies Proficiency with learning management systems and basic instructional technology Strong organizational abilities, including timely grading, accurate record‑keeping, and adherence to academic policies Ability to work effectively with faculty, staff, and students Commitment to Concord University’s mission and to supporting student success in foundational coursework Required Experience Type of experience Needed Experience teaching Quantitative Reasoning, College Algebra, and/or Elementary Statistics preferred Amount of Experience Needed (Months/Years) More than 2 years Posting Detail Information Close Date Open Until Filled Yes Additional Information Requirements for Completed Application.- Letter of application- CV- Unofficial copy of transcripts (The selected candidate will be required to submit official copies of transcripts before time of appointment- Three references and their contact information (including a current address, phone number and e-mail address) Quick Link to Posting https://jobs.concord.edu/postings/1602 Posting Supplemental Questions Required fields are indicated with an asterisk (*). Edwards School of Medicine’s Department of Cardiovascular Services is seeking a board-certified/board-eligible Advanced Heart Failure Cardiologist to join our growing faculty. The ideal candidate will bring expertise in the diagnosis and management of complex heart failure, including pre- and post-transplant care, mechanical circulatory support, and advanced therapies. This role is part of a dynamic and expanding academic cardiology program in a collegial, team-based environment. Faculty physicians enjoy access to state-of-the-art facilities and strong institutional support for both clinical and academic growth. Participate in inpatient rounding every 6th weekend, with support from cardiology fellows (no year-round call requirement). Teach and mentor general cardiology fellows, residents, and medical students in both formal and informal settings. Engage in scholarly activity including quality improvement initiatives, clinical research, and collaboration with Marshall’s translational and biomedical sciences programs. Concord University is a small liberal arts college located in scenic Athens, WV near Pipestem State Park. Our campus offers a close-knit academic community and a beautiful rural setting that fosters engaged teaching, scholarship, and collegial collaboration. Our rural location provides a welcoming community with opportunities for meaningful faculty-student interaction inside and outside the classroom.Application ProcessApplicants should submitCover letter addressing teaching philosophyCurriculum vitaeEvidence of teaching (student evaluations or other documentation if available)Contact information for three professional referencesApplications will only be accepted through Concord University’s online application site at https://jobs.concord.edu/. Review of applications will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled.Concord University is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and encourages all qualified candidates to apply.We are committed to attracting and retaining quality faculty and staff. In doing so, Concord University offers outstanding benefit packages including:Holidays – Employees receive 13-14 Paid Holidays AnnuallyHealth Insurance – Concord University offers health insurance through West Virginia Public Employees Insurance Agency (PEIA).Tuition and Fee Waivers- Professional development and education opportunities including tuition waiver program for employees, spouse, and eligible dependents.Retirement Plans – TIAA’s automatic retirement plan is a 401(a) plan into which six (6) percent of the employee’s total salary is automatically withheld pre-tax and deposited into the employee’s TIAA retirement account. The university matches the employees 6% contributionLife Insurance – Basic term life insurance ($10,000) at no cost and may purchase optional life insurance coverage with pre-tax earnings.Mountaineer Flexible Benefits. This is an IRS approved, tax free account that saves money on eligible health, medical, dental, and dependent care expenses.Annual Increment Pay Posting Details Position Information Job Category Faculty Position Title Assistant Professor of Chemistry (Tenure Track) Working Title Assistant Professor of Chemistry (Tenure Track) Scheduled Hours Per Week FLSA Status Exempt Job Summary Job Summary The Department of Physical and Environmental Sciences at Concord University is accepting applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Chemistry. The position requires the ability to develop and teach the organic chemistry sequence with lab, introductory chemistry labs, and general chemistry. A Ph.D. in chemistry or a closely related field is required, although applicants who are ABD or with different qualifications may be considered for a visiting appointment. Appointment at higher rank may be possible for well-qualified candidates.The Department values and actively supports innovative teaching and participation in undergraduate research and seeks candidates with similar ideals. The chemistry program supports majors in chemistry (including a biochemistry option and a geochemistry option), biology, health sciences, nursing, science education, and environmental geosciences. The Department maintains a diverse array of instrumentation for teaching and undergraduate research, including GC, GC-MS, ICP-OES, fluorimeter, micro-XRF, XRD, HPLC, SCF extractor, microplate reader, Raman, IR, UV-Vis, FT-IR, potentiostat/galvanostat, AFM, polarizing microscopes, thin section/materials prep laboratory, microwave reactor, plasma sputter and vacuum carbon coaters, vacuum spin coater, a benchtop NMR, and an electron microprobe (EPMA) as part of the Concord Materials and Rare Earth Elements Analysis Center. Department faculty lead or co-lead numerous externally funded projects and other collaborative initiatives in geosciences, physics, and chemistry.Concord University is a public, liberal-arts institution with an enrollment of approximately 1800 students. The University is in a scenic, small-town setting in the mountains of southern West Virginia with access to year-round outdoor recreation activities. Duties and Responsibilities Duty/Responsibility The candidate will teach a 12 contact-hour load/semester and will be expected to engage in professional development that enhances their teaching, develop organic chemistry lecture and lab experiences, assume a role in formal and informal student mentoring, supervise undergraduate research, and participate in departmental activities and University governance including contributions to programmatic assessment efforts. The successful candidate will participate in routine upkeep and maintenance of laboratory facilities and engage in safe and ethical laboratory practices as a role model to students % of Time 100% Education/Knowledge Minimum Education Doctorate Required Licenses/Certification Position requires a Ph.D. for assistant professor rank, or M.S. for instructor rank. Required Skills Candidates with a record of teaching, scholarship, and demonstrable commitment to undergraduate mentoring preferred. Demonstrated potential for scholarly research, publication, or professional developme
